{{Nav Games Header}}

<b>Save data</b> in <i>[[Hollow Knight: Silksong]]</i> records the player's progress in the game, and their preferences in the menu. It includes the four profiles that the player can save (plus their [[Save Data (Silksong)/Save Points#Auto Saves|auto saves]]), as well as [[#Game Preferences|settings]], [[Controls (Silksong)|controls]], [[Achievements (Silksong)|achievements]], [[Menu Styles (Silksong)|menu styles]], and whether [[Steel Soul Mode (Silksong)|Steel Soul mode]] is unlocked.

== Game Progress ==
* The four save profiles
* [[Save Data (Silksong)/Save Points#Auto Saves|Auto save]] history for each save profile
* Shared game state like the [[Map and Quill (Silksong)#Map Pins|Map pin]] visibility mode, whether [[Steel Soul Mode (Silksong)|Steel Soul mode]] is unlocked, and which [[Achievements (Silksong)|achievements]] have been fulfilled

|}

=== Files ===
* <code>shared.dat</code> contains only [[#Shared Keys|shared game state]]
* <code>user#.dat</code> 1–4 are save profiles
** <code>user#.dat.bak1</code> 1–4 are backups created before saving a profile
** <code>user#_1.0.12345.dat</code> 1–4 are created before saving a profile belonging to an earlier patch
* <code>Restore_Points#</code> 1–4 are folders containing [[Save Data (Silksong)/Save Points#Auto Saves|auto saves]] for the numbered save profile
** <code>restoreData#.dat</code> 1–99 are auto saves
** <code>NODELrestoreData#.dat</code> 1–99 are auto saves protected from [[Save Data (Silksong)/Save Points#Auto Saves|auto-deletion]]

=== Shared Keys ===
Game state shared between all save profiles is stored as a list of named keys inside <code>shared.dat</code>. Each key has a value, which is treated as <code>0</code> by default if the key is missing.

== Game Preferences ==
* Game, audio, video, controller and keyboard settings
* The selected [[Menu Styles (Silksong)|menu style]]
* Which save profile was last loaded
* Window size, position, and monitor

=== Preference Keys ===
Preferences are stored as a list of named keys. They are usually inside a file named <code>prefs</code>, except on Windows, where they are stored in the [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windows_Registry Registry] instead. Each key has a value which controls a corresponding in-game setting.

{| class="article-table mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" width="100%"
| colspan="3" |
|-
! style="width: 16rem;" | Key
! style="width: 16rem;" | Description
! style="min-width: 12rem;" | Values
|-
| <code>AppleMFi</code>
| {{MissingInfo}}
| <code>0</code> {{MissingInfo}}<br><code>1</code> {{MissingInfo}}
|-
| <code>CameraShakeSetting</code>
| <i>Game → Camera Shake</i>
| <code>0</code> On<br><code>1</code> Reduced<br><code>2</code> Off
|-
| <code>ControllerSWITCH_JOYCON_DUAL</code>
| <i>Controller → Remap Controls</i><br><small>(with a [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nintendo_Switch_Pro_Controller Nintendo Switch Pro Controller] connected)</small>
| JSON string
|-
| <code>ControllerXBOX_ONE</code>
| <i>Controller → Remap Controls</i><br><small>(with an [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox_Wireless_Controller Xbox Wireless Controller] connected)</small>
| JSON string
|-
| <code>GameBackers</code>
| <i>Game → Backer Credits</i>
| <code>0</code> Off<br><code>1</code> On
|-
| <code>GameLang</code>
| <i>Game → Language</i>
| <code>37</code> German<br><code>44</code> English<br><code>57</code> Spanish<br><code>82</code> French<br><code>105</code> Italian<br><code>109</code> Japanese<br><code>117</code> Korean<br><code>147</code> Brazilian Portuguese<br><code>154</code> Russian<br><code>199</code> Simplified Chinese<br>
|-
| <code>GameLangSet</code>
| Whether player has chosen a language on first launch.
| <code>0</code> No (will ask next launch)<br><code>1</code> Yes
|-
| <code>GameNativePopups</code>
| <i>Game → Show Achievements</i>
| <code>0</code> Off<br><code>1</code> On
|-
| <code>HudScaleSetting</code>
| <i>Game → HUD Appearance</i><ref group="Note">The "Off" setting is never actually saved, so it resets on game exit.</ref>
| <code>0</code> Large<br><code>1</code> Small
|-
| <code>KeyAttack</code>
| <i>Keyboard → Attack</i>
| Keycode (eg. <code>X</code>)
|-
| <code>KeyCast</code>
| <i>Keyboard → Bind</i>
| Keycode (eg. <code>A</code>)
|-
| <code>KeyDash</code>
| <i>Keyboard → Sprint</i>
| Keycode (eg. <code>C</code>)
|-
| <code>KeyDown</code>
| <i>Keyboard → Down</i>
| Keycode (eg. <code>DownArrow</code>)
|-
| <code>KeyDreamnail</code>
| <i>Keyboard → Needolin</i>
| Keycode (eg. <code>D</code>)
|-
| <code>KeyInventory</code>
| <i>Keyboard → Inventory</i>
| Keycode (eg. <code>I</code>)
|-
| <code>KeyInventoryJournal</code>
| <i>Keyboard → Journal</i>
| Keycode (eg. <code>J</code>)
|-
| <code>KeyInventoryMap</code>

== Save Points ==
{{Main|Save Data (Silksong)/Save Points}}

<b>Save points</b> refer to any event that saves the game normally, overwriting the current profile. [[Hornet (Silksong)|Hornet]] will respawn at her last save point when she dies, and when the profile is loaded. Whenever a save point is triggered, an animated icon spins in the lower-right corner of the screen for a fraction of a second.

The most obvious save points are the [[Bench (Silksong)|Benches]] throughout [[Pharloom]], but there are many other events that save the game automatically. <i>Silksong</i> features three different types of save points:
* [[File:Tools Prompt.png|frameless |link=|alt=|24px]] <b>[[Bench (Silksong)|Bench saves]]</b>: Manual save points
* [[File:Icon SS Auto Save.png|frameless|link=|alt=|24px]] <b>[[Save Data (Silksong)/Save Points#Auto Saves|Auto saves]]</b>: Automatic save points that are recorded on the <i>Auto Saves</i> menu
* [[File:Icon SS Save.png|frameless|link=|alt=|24px]] <b>Temporary auto saves</b>: Automatic save points that simply save the game
